     6 Strategic Database Indexing Plan (Advisory)
    You indicated an intention to add database indexes to further improve query performance across frequently
    used tables. The following indexing strategy is customized for the CIRIL CRM reporting and lead query
    profiles:
    Query Profile Bottleneck
    The reports join 6 tables on foreign keys and apply range scans on leads.created_at:
    SELECT rd.city_id, rd.selected_requirement_id FROM leads l
    INNER JOIN requirements_details rd ON l.id = rd.lead_id
    INNER JOIN client_details cd ON l.id = cd.lead_id
    INNER JOIN financial_details fd ON l.id = fd.lead_id
    WHERE l.created_at BETWEEN '...' AND '...' AND rd.city_id IS NOT NULL;
    Recommended Composite Indexes
    Table Index Definition Query Impact & Benefit
    leads idx_leads_created_status
    (created_at, leadStatus)
    Transforms the historical date range query into a fast B-
    Tree index range seek. MySQL quickly identifies the
    lead rows matching the date boundaries without a full
    table scan.
    requirements_details idx_req_lead_city_ver
    (lead_id, city_id,
    selected_requirement_id)
    Covering Index: Resolves the join on lead_id, filters
    city_id IS NOT NULL, and retrieves
    selected_requirement_id entirely from the index tree
    without touching table data blocks on disk.
    client_details idx_client_details_lead_id
    (lead_id)
    Accelerates the INNER JOIN on l.id = cd.lead_id
    from an un-indexed scan to an O(1) indexed key lookup.
    financial_details idx_financial_details_lead_id
    (lead_id)
    Accelerates the INNER JOIN on l.id = fd.lead_id
    from an un-indexed scan to an O(1) indexed key lookup.
    Ready-to-Execute SQL Script (phpMyAdmin / MySQL Console)
    -- Execute via phpMyAdmin or MySQL CLI during low-traffic periods
    ALTER TABLE `leads`
      ADD INDEX `idx_leads_created_status` (`created_at`, `leadStatus`);
    ALTER TABLE `requirements_details`
      ADD INDEX `idx_req_lead_city_ver` (`lead_id`, `city_id`, `selected_requirement_id`);
    ALTER TABLE `client_details`
      ADD INDEX `idx_client_details_lead_id` (`lead_id`);
    ALTER TABLE `financial_details`
      ADD INDEX `idx_financial_details_lead_id` (`lead_id`);

     Performance Outcome: Adding these indexes will reduce multi-table join query latency from ~25ms down
    to ~2ms, providing future-proof query execution as lead records grow into the hundreds of thousands.

### What I approve

The following changes are appropriate for the identified reporting bottleneck:

These are targeted reporting changes; they do not inherently change lead creation, ownership, or assignment. The resulting table structure should remain compatible with existing exports.

### Why I cannot approve the whole document

| Location | Issue requiring correction |
|---|---|
| **Pages 1–2** | “RESOLVED & VERIFIED,” “0.42 ms,” and “60,000× faster” are not supported by reproducible test results in the document. Fast recorded queries support the diagnosis, but do not prove every remaining millisecond was spent in that loop. |
| **Page 3** | The replacement begins with `} else {`, but the displayed original block starts *after* the existing closing brace. Replacing the shown block literally can introduce an extra brace and break PHP syntax. Exact replacement boundaries are necessary. |
| **Page 4** | The SQL contains `...`, so this is an illustrative snippet—not complete deployable code. Existing joins, filters, view variables, sorting and totals must be retained. |
| **Pages 3–4** | `if ($cityId)` drops zero/empty IDs, and changing the SQL condition to `IS NOT NULL` changes its semantics. Normally valid positive IDs make these differences irrelevant, but equivalence requires checking the data. |

| **Pages 7–8** | The index statements are presented as ready to execute without checking existing indexes, actual production schema, query plans or database version. The promised reduction from ~25 ms to ~2 ms is unverified. |

Also, the existing filtered method directly inserts request values into SQL. **This patch does not address that existing security concern**; parameter binding should be reviewed separately.

### Database indexing: defer it

The indexes are plausible candidates, **not a necessary part of fixing this timeout**.

Before adding them, inspect `SHOW INDEX` and `EXPLAIN` on the production database. Existing indexes may already cover the joins, and index usefulness depends on column order and query shape. Index creation also has operational costs and can involve locking. [MySQL index documentation](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/26.7/en/multiple-column-indexes.html), [online DDL documentation](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/innodb-online-ddl-operations.html).

        public function reports()
        {
            $orgId = Auth()->user()->orgId;
            try {
                if (Auth()->user()->roleId == 1) {
                    $fromdate = config('globalConfig.defalutDateforLeads');
                    $todate = date('Y-m-d');
                    $leads = Lead::join('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('requirements_details', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')

                        ->select('leads.id AS LId', 'leads.created_at as Cdate', 'leads.accepted_datetime', 'leads.leadStatus', 'leads.assigned_to', 'leads.assigned_orgid', 'client_details.*', 'requirements_details.*', 'financial_details.*')
                        ->orderBy('leads.id', 'desc')
                        ->get();
                }
    
                return view('Leads/newdesign/Reports/report', ['leads' => $leads, 'from' => $fromdate, 'to' => $todate]);
            } catch (\Exception $e) {
                return $e->getMessage();
            }
        }

        public function getLeadData($where = null, $category = null, $join = null, $fromdate = null, $todate = null)
        {
            $sql = "select * from leads l
            inner join client_details cd on l.id=cd.lead_id
            inner join requirements_details rd  on l.id=rd.lead_id
            inner join financial_details fd  on l.id=fd.lead_id
            inner join cities c on c.cityId=rd.city_id
            inner join verticals v on v.verId=rd.selected_requirement_id
            inner join lead_status_types lst on lst.id=l.leadStatus
            $join
            where  l.created_at between '" . $fromdate . ' 00:00:00' . "' and '" . $todate . ' 23:59:59' . "' and rd.$category is not null $where";
            $leadData = DB::select($sql);
            return $leadData;
        }

            }
            $leadsData = collect($this->getLeadData($where, 'city_id', $join, $request->datefrom, $request->dateto));

    namespace App\Models\Settings;

    class VerticalModel extends Authenticatable

        /**

        protected $table = 'verticals';

            'verName', 'fields', 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'createdBy', 'updatedBy'

        public function verticalWiseTotalLeadsGiven($filters)
        {
            $verticals = $this->selectRaw("verticals.verName, zones.zoneName, COUNT(leads.id) as leads_count")
                ->leftJoin('requirements_details', 'verticals.verId', '=', 'requirements_details.selected_requirement_id')
                ->leftJoin('leads', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('lead_status_types', 'leads.leadStatus', '=', 'lead_status_types.id')
                ->leftJoin('zones', 'requirements_details.req_zone', '=', 'zones.zoneId')
                ->groupBy('verticals.verName', 'requirements_details.req_zone');
    
            if (!empty($filters['zone_id'])) {
                $verticals->where('zones.zoneId', $filters['zone_id']);
            }
            // for date filter
            $leads_from = $filters['leads_from'] ?? '';
            $leads_to = $filters['leads_to'] ?? '';
            if (!empty($leads_from) && !empty($leads_to)) {
                $verticals->whereBetween('leads.created_at', [$leads_from . ' 00:00:00', $leads_to . ' 23:59:59']);
            }
    
            $verticalLeads = DB::table($verticals, 'vl')
                ->selectRaw('GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT vl.verName ORDER BY vl.verName) as xAxises, vl.zoneName, GROUP_CONCAT(vl.leads_count ORDER BY vl.verName) as totals')
                ->groupBy('vl.zoneName');
            $v = $verticalLeads->get();
            return $this->getCorrectData($v);
        }
    
        public function verticalWiseTotalLeadsReceived($filters)
        {
            $verticals = $this->selectRaw("verticals.verName, zones.zoneName, COUNT(distinct(leads.id)) as leads_count")
                ->leftJoin('requirements_details', 'verticals.verId', '=', 'requirements_details.selected_requirement_id')
                ->leftJoin('leads', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->leftJoin('lead_status_types', 'leads.leadStatus', '=', 'lead_status_types.id')
                ->leftJoin('company', 'leads.assigned_to', '=', 'company.companyName')
                ->leftJoin('users', 'company.id', '=', 'users.orgId')
                ->leftJoin('zones', 'requirements_details.req_zone', '=', 'zones.zoneId')
                ->groupBy('verticals.verName', 'requirements_details.req_zone')
                ->where('leads.accepted', '=', 1)
                ->orderBy('verticals.verName', 'desc')
                ->where(function ($query) {
                    $query->orWhere('leads.leadStatus', '2')
                        ->orWhere('leads.leadStatus', '3')

    page()
    h('4. Why the change addresses the timeout')
    p('The old loop visits every lead, then every vertical, and repeatedly filters the entire retrieved collection to count the same city/vertical combination. Its work grows roughly as O(N squared times V). The new code counts each joined row once in a PHP array, then builds the existing result matrix once per distinct city: O(N + C times V). N is joined rows, C unique cities, and V vertical records.')
    p('The patch deliberately counts joined rows, not distinct leads. Duplicate join rows were counted previously and remain counted. It retains first-seen city ordering, vertical iteration order, zero values for absent combinations, vertical-name keys, existing verticalSortFn(), totals calculation, and view parameters.')
    p('Normal integer IDs and canonical numeric-string IDs share PHP array keys, matching the existing comparisons. No truthiness filter is introduced: zero IDs are not silently dropped. Noncanonical ID strings such as leading-zero strings, floats, or malformed values can differ from Laravel loose comparisons; verify production column types and ID cleanliness before approval. The existing inner joins imply valid referenced IDs but are not a substitute for inspecting schema/data.')
    p('Both existing SQL statements and their selected columns are intentionally preserved. reportVerticalFilter() still uses SELECT * and the existing truthy selected_requirement_id condition. This avoids changing SQL semantics or resolving same-name-column behavior as part of an emergency performance patch. The second identical SQL execution is removed; every tally now uses one consistent query snapshot.')
    h('5. Changes intentionally not included')
    p('Permissions and non-super-admin behavior remain unchanged. The original default method only defines its leads collection inside roleId == 1; this patch does not invent an empty-report policy or broaden access. Validate intended authorized roles before production deployment. Broader authorization hardening is a separate task.')
    p('Existing raw request interpolation in reportVerticalFilter() remains a security concern. Parameterized SQL and validation should be reviewed separately; this performance patch is not a security sign-off. Other report endpoints, cron tasks, SMTP, lead creation, and database schema are outside scope.')
    p('No index script is supplied. Query timings do not justify adding indexes as the primary timeout fix. Inspect actual production indexes and EXPLAIN output before any independent indexing change. No performance guarantee of sub-millisecond computation or sub-second HTTP response is made.')

        $orgId = Auth()->user()->orgId;

            if (Auth()->user()->roleId == 1) {
                $fromdate = config('globalConfig.defalutDateforLeads');
                $todate = date('Y-m-d');
                $leads = Lead::join('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                    ->join('requirements_details', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                    ->join('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                    ->whereBetween('leads.created_at', [$fromdate . ' 00:00:00', $todate . ' 23:59:59'])
                    ->select('leads.id AS LId', 'leads.created_at as Cdate', 'leads.accepted_datetime', 'leads.leadStatus', 'leads.assigned_to', 'leads.assigned_orgid', 'client_details.*', 'requirements_details.*', 'financial_details.*')
                    ->orderBy('leads.id', 'desc')
                    ->get();
            }

            return view('Leads/newdesign/Reports/report', ['leads' => $leads, 'from' => $fromdate, 'to' => $todate]);
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            return $e->getMessage();
        }
    }

    public function getLeadData($where = null, $category = null, $join = null, $fromdate = null, $todate = null)
    {
        $sql = "select * from leads l
        inner join client_details cd on l.id=cd.lead_id 
        inner join requirements_details rd  on l.id=rd.lead_id
        inner join financial_details fd  on l.id=fd.lead_id 
        inner join cities c on c.cityId=rd.city_id        
        inner join verticals v on v.verId=rd.selected_requirement_id  
        inner join lead_status_types lst on lst.id=l.leadStatus         
        $join
        where  l.created_at between '" . $fromdate . ' 00:00:00' . "' and '" . $todate . ' 23:59:59' . "' and rd.$category is not null $where";
        $leadData = DB::select($sql);
        return $leadData;
    }

        $cities = CityModel::orderBy('cityName')->get();
        $verticals = VerticalModel::all();
        $status = Lead_status_type::all();

        $result = [];
        foreach ($queryResult as $c) {
            foreach ($verticals as $v) {
                $result[$c->city_id][$v->verName] = $leads->where('selected_requirement_id', $v->verId)->where('city_id', $c->city_id)->count();
            }
        }
        $sortedCityList = $this->verticalSortFn($result);
        $c = collect($sortedCityList);
        foreach ($verticals as $v) {
            $total[$v->verName] = $c->pluck($v->verName)->sum();
        }
        return view('Leads/newdesign/Reports/report_verticalwise', [
            'results' => $sortedCityList,
            'v' => $verticals,
            'cities' => $cities,
            'totals' => $total,
            'statuses' => $status,
            'inputs' => $input,
            'errors' => $error
        ]);
    }
    public function reportsZonalWise(Request $request)
    {
        try {
            $fromdate = config('globalConfig.defalutDateforLeads');
            $todate = date('Y-m-d');
            $input['datefrom'] = $fromdate;
            $input['dateto'] = $todate;

            $cities = CityModel::all();
            $leadsData = Lead::join('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->join('requirements_details', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->join('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                ->join('cities', 'cities.cityId', '=', 'requirements_details.city_id')
                ->join('lead_status_types', 'leads.leadStatus', '=', 'lead_status_types.id')
                ->join('verticals', 'verticals.verId', '=', 'requirements_details.selected_requirement_id')
                ->whereBetween('leads.created_at', [$fromdate . ' 00:00:00', $todate . ' 23:59:59'])
                ->whereNotNull('requirements_details.city_id')
                ->select('leads.*', 'client_details.*', 'requirements_details.*', 'financial_details.*')
                ->orderBy('leads.id', 'desc')
                ->get();

            $sql = "select rd.city_id as city,count(city_id) as total from leads l
                    inner join client_details cd on l.id=cd.lead_id 
                    inner join requirements_details rd  on l.id=rd.lead_id
                    inner join financial_details fd  on l.id=fd.lead_id  
                    inner join cities c on c.cityId=rd.city_id        
                    inner join verticals v on v.verId=rd.selected_requirement_id  
                    inner join lead_status_types lst on lst.id=l.leadStatus                                      
                    where l.created_at between '" . $fromdate . ' 00:00:00' . "' and '" . $todate . ' 23:59:59' . "' and rd.city_id is not null group by rd.city_id ";
            $leads =  collect(DB::select($sql))->keyBy('city');
            foreach ($cities as $city) {
                if ($leads->has($city->cityId)) {
                    $result[$city->cityName]['Total'] = $leads[$city->cityId]->total;
                } else {
                    $result[$city->cityName]['Total'] = 0;
                }
                $result[$city->cityName]['Active'] =  $leadsData->where('city_id', $city->cityId)->where('leadStatus', 2)->count();
                $result[$city->cityName]['Concluded'] = $leadsData->where('city_id', $city->cityId)->where('leadStatus', 3)->count();
                $result[$city->cityName]['Cancelled'] = $leadsData->where('city_id', $city->cityId)->where('leadStatus', 5)->count();
            }
            $zones = ZoneModel::all();
            return view('Leads/newdesign/Reports/report_zonalwise', ['results' => $result, 'zones' => $zones, 'inputs' => $input]);
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            return $e->getMessage();
        }
    }

    public function citySortFn($leads_unsort)
    {
        $sortCityList = config('globalConfig.sortCitiesList');
        $matched = [];
        $unMatched = [];
        $i = 0;
        $j = 0;
        foreach ($leads_unsort as $k => $v) {
            if (isset($sortCityList)) {
                if (in_array($v['city'], $sortCityList)) {
                    $matched[$i]['city'] = $v['city'];
                    $matched[$i]['total'] = $v['total'];
                    $i++;
                } else {
                    $unMatched[$j]['city'] = $v['city'];
                    $unMatched[$j]['total'] = $v['total'];
                    $j++;
                }
            } else {
                $leads = $leads_unsort;
            }
        }
        $leads = array_merge($matched, $unMatched);
        return $leads;
    }
    public function verticalSortFn($leads_unsort)
    {
        $sortCityList = config('globalConfig.sortCitiesList');
        $keys = array_keys($leads_unsort);
        $common = array_intersect($sortCityList, $keys);
        $diff = array_diff($keys, $sortCityList);
        $sortedArray = array_values(array_merge($common, $diff));
        $result = [];
        foreach ($sortedArray as $key => $value) {
            $result[$value] = $leads_unsort[$value];
        }
        return $result;
    }
}

    # PDF Processing Guide
    
    ## Overview
    
    This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see reference.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read forms.md and follow its instructions.
    
    ## Quick Start
    
    ```python
    from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    
    # Read a PDF
    reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")
    
    # Extract text
    text = ""
    for page in reader.pages:
        text += page.extract_text()
    ```
    
    ## Python Libraries
    
    ### pypdf - Basic Operations
    
    #### Merge PDFs
    ```python
    from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader
    
    writer = PdfWriter()
    for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
        reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
        for page in reader.pages:
            writer.add_page(page)
    
    with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
    ```
    
    #### Split PDF
    ```python
    reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
        writer = PdfWriter()
        writer.add_page(page)
        with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
            writer.write(output)
    ```
    
    #### Extract Metadata
    ```python
    reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    meta = reader.metadata
    print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
    print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
    print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
    print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
    ```
    
    #### Rotate Pages
    ```python
    reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    writer = PdfWriter()
    
    page = reader.pages[0]
    page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
    writer.add_page(page)
    
    with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
    ```
    
    ### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction
    
    #### Extract Text with Layout
    ```python
    import pdfplumber
    
    with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
        for page in pdf.pages:
            text = page.extract_text()
            print(text)
    ```
    
    #### Extract Tables
    ```python
    with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
        for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
            tables = page.extract_tables()
            for j, table in enumerate(tables):
                print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
                for row in table:
                    print(row)
    ```
    
    #### Advanced Table Extraction
    ```python
    import pandas as pd
    
    with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
        all_tables = []
        for page in pdf.pages:
            tables = page.extract_tables()
            for table in tables:
                if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                    df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                    all_tables.append(df)
    
    # Combine all tables
    if all_tables:
        combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
        combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
    ```
    
    ### reportlab - Create PDFs
    
    #### Basic PDF Creation
    ```python
    from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
    
    c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
    width, height = letter
    
    # Add text
    c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
    c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")
    
    # Add a line
    c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)
    
    # Save
    c.save()
    ```
    
    #### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
    ```python
    from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
    from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
    from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet
    
    doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
    styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
    story = []
    
    # Add content
    title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
    story.append(title)
    story.append(Spacer(1, 12))
    
    body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
    story.append(body)
    story.append(PageBreak())
    
    # Page 2
    story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
    story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))
    
    # Build PDF
    doc.build(story)
    ```
    
    ## Command-Line Tools
    
    ### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
    ```bash
    # Extract text
    pdftotext input.pdf output.txt
    
    # Extract text preserving layout
    pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt
    
    # Extract specific pages
    pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
    ```
    
    ### qpdf
    ```bash
    # Merge PDFs
    qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf
    
    # Split pages
    qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
    qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf
    
    # Rotate pages
    qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees
    
    # Remove password
    qpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
    ```
    
    ### pdftk (if available)
    ```bash
    # Merge
    pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf
    
    # Split
    pdftk input.pdf burst
    
    # Rotate
    pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
    ```
    
    ## Common Tasks
    
    ### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
    ```python
    # Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
    import pytesseract
    from pdf2image import convert_from_path
    
    # Convert PDF to images
    images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')
    
    # OCR each page
    text = ""
    for i, image in enumerate(images):
        text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
        text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
        text += "\n\n"
    
    print(text)
    ```
    
    ### Add Watermark
    ```python
    from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    
    # Create watermark (or load existing)
    watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]
    
    # Apply to all pages
    reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    writer = PdfWriter()
    
    for page in reader.pages:
        page.merge_page(watermark)
        writer.add_page(page)
    
    with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
    ```
    
    ### Extract Images
    ```bash
    # Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
    pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix
    
    # This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
    ```
    
    ### Password Protection
    ```python
    from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    
    reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
    writer = PdfWriter()
    
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)
    
    # Add password
    writer.encrypt("userpassword", "ownerpassword")
    
    with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
    ```
    
    ## Quick Reference
    
    | Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
    |------|-----------|--------------|
    | Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
    | Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
    | Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
    | Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
    | Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
    | Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
    | OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |

    The October request returned 98 leads for the tested member. None was created in October: the returned dates run
    from 31 May 2023 to 3 September 2026. This is a confirmed date-filter defect, not a failed login or an inability to create
    a download.
    The query combines company assignment and lead ownership with an ungrouped OR condition. SQL applies the date
    condition to the ownership branch only. Leads assigned to the member company bypass the requested dates. The
    same pattern exists in the default lead list and the selected-date list.
    CSV and XLSX both exported the 98 wrong upstream rows. Separate browser tests reduced the current table to one
    matching lead and then zero leads; both export formats followed those client filters and produced matching lead ID
    sets. Export row selection is working in these observed cases. The report does not classify every export function as
    broken.
    There is still an independent export consistency issue: CSV has 19 columns and XLSX has 18. CSV includes both
    copies of Lead Status; XLSX excludes the hidden copy. Both formats include non-business action/preview fields. A
    common export schema and an applied-date guard are proposed.

    5. Proposed backend replacement
    C1 consolidates both entry points, so fixing the date-selection route cannot leave the default/reset route with the same
    ungrouped OR defect. It validates only the two lead-list fields, returns an empty table on invalid input, and does not
    change shared validator behavior elsewhere.
    Same-day ranges are allowed. A future end date is allowed so a full current-month range such as 1-31 October is valid
    on 26 October. This is an explicit proposed date policy. The end predicate is midnight after the selected To date, which
    includes fractional seconds on the last day without truncation.
    The application timezone is Asia/Kolkata. The proposal assumes stored lead timestamps use the same established
    convention as the current date comparisons. Confirm the production storage convention; if timestamps are UTC,
    convert date boundaries to UTC before comparison without changing the user-facing dates.
    Null or empty organization IDs do not grant access to every unassigned lead. The creator branch still applies. This is a
    deliberate guard for accounts without an organization and must be included in the authorization review; normal member
    accounts keep their current company-or-creator rule.
    No catch block returns raw database exception text. A runtime failure follows Laravel error handling; no completed
    table is returned for export. Production debug/error handling should follow the existing deployment policy.

    Page 9
    6. Proposed view and export changes
    The proposal keeps browser-side DataTables exports because the current table loads the complete authorized result
    set (serverSide=false). Every format will export all currently filtered rows across all pages, not just the visible page or a
    selected row subset. If server-side paging is introduced later, implement an authorized server export using the same
    query contract; these client options alone cannot export rows that were never loaded.
    The shared business-column list includes one plain Lead Status, Lead Stage Status, giver and receiver company,
    receiver manager, area, ageing, vertical, location, zone, Accepted Date and Remark Histories. It excludes Actions,
    Preview, the editable status cell, and the interactive Remarks icon column. This changes the CSV/XLSX schema
    intentionally; management should approve downstream spreadsheet/import compatibility.
    The action wrapper blocks all formats when input dates differ from applied server dates, when validation fails, or when
    the filtered table has zero rows. Users receive a clear message rather than a misleading stale file or empty download.
    XLSX requires browser JSZip; no PHP Zip/GD installation is required for this browser-based export. CSV remains
    available if only JSZip fails.
    Filename dates come from the applied server range, not editable draft fields. Filenames identify the date range but do
    not encode every dropdown/global search; the exported rows still honor those active client filters. Both formats use a
    common text formatter, remove HTML, and prefix spreadsheet-formula-like text. The older installed Buttons version
    does not support the newer escapeExcelFormula setting, so the formatter implements this explicitly.
    The custom action signature targets the observed Buttons 2.3.2 API. An upgrade to a newer major version must
    re-check its action callback and asynchronous behavior. Existing numeric-looking strings and leading zeros need
    round-trip tests in Excel; a fully typed workbook schema is outside this proposal.

    8. Account behavior and regression protection
     Account / data condition
    Expected result after proposal
    Admin roleId 1
    All joined leads within the requested creation dates; no member company restriction
    added.
    Member: assigned company matches
    Only assigned-company leads inside the requested period, even when another user
    created them.
    Member: creator matches
    Own created leads inside the requested period, even when assigned elsewhere.
    Member: both branches match
    One joined result per existing join behavior; no duplicate introduced by OR grouping.
    Check related-table multiplicity separately.
    Member: neither branch matches
    Excluded, even when created inside the requested period.

    Only creator-visible leads. Unassigned leads belonging to other creators are excluded.

    Zero rows and a no-match export message. Do not expose another company's October
    leads to fill the report.
    Default entry / Reset
    Configured default From date through today; both dates apply to every visibility branch.
    Different active member roles
    Apply the current roleId != 1 member rule; validate with representatives of each
    configured role before release.
    Unauthenticated visitor
    Existing auth middleware remains responsible for rejection/redirect. No export bypass
    route added.
    Shared-code limits
    The shared validateToFromDate helper remains unchanged because it serves dashboard, reporting and mining
    screens. Removing unrelated required fields from that helper globally could affect those callers. This report fixes the
    lead list locally and records the shared-helper cleanup as a separate review item.
    Wildcard selections from detail tables and inner-join cardinality are preserved to keep this change focused. The query
    filters ownership with leads.user_id, independent of any same-named joined columns. Audit joined row multiplicity and
    N+1 view lookups separately if counts or performance remain problematic.

    10.1 Controlled implementation and approvals
    Rollout sequence
    1. Assign a developer and QA owner; approve the creation-date definition, same-day/future-end policy, no-match
    behavior, and common export column schema. Confirm null-organization account policy and timestamp storage
    convention.
    2. Compare baseline hashes and take version-controlled backups of the three files. Apply C1 and V1-V5 together on
    staging, then F1. Keep routes, roles, data and shared validator unchanged. Run PHP syntax and Blade compilation
    checks on that environment.
    3. Complete the account and boundary matrix. Parse actual CSV and XLSX files; compare lead ID sets, dates and
    columns. Include multi-page, special-character and dependency-failure tests. Record environment, user role, request
    URL, expected/actual counts and file hashes.
    4. Obtain business-owner and QA acceptance. Deploy the reviewed revision using the normal release process.
    Clear/rebuild compiled Blade views as required by that deployment; do not run blanket database commands or broad
    cache deletion.
    5. Re-check the tested account and representative admin/member accounts. Monitor export failures, validation errors,
    query timings and unexpected row counts. Keep evidence limited to authorized reviewers.
    Rollback and closure
    Rollback restores the prior three-file revision and refreshes compiled views through the normal deployment process. No
    data migration is required. Restoring the previous revision also restores the known date-filter defect; mark reports from
    that version as unreliable for date-specific use.
    Close CRM-FILTER-2026-001 only after code approval, evidence for the test matrix, scoped export parity,
    shared-screen smoke checks and acceptance of the export schema. Until then, status remains Confirmed / Proposed
    fix pending.

    5. Proposed backend replacement
    C1 consolidates both entry points, so fixing the date-selection route cannot leave the default/reset route with the same
    ungrouped OR defect. It validates only the two lead-list fields, returns an empty table on invalid input, and does not
    change shared validator behavior elsewhere.
    Same-day ranges are allowed. A future end date is allowed so a full current-month range such as 1-31 October is valid
    on 26 October. This is an explicit proposed date policy. The end predicate is midnight after the selected To date, which
    includes fractional seconds on the last day without truncation.
    The application timezone is Asia/Kolkata. The proposal assumes stored lead timestamps use the same established
    convention as the current date comparisons. Confirm the production storage convention; if timestamps are UTC,
    convert date boundaries to UTC before comparison without changing the user-facing dates.
    Null or empty organization IDs do not grant access to every unassigned lead. The creator branch still applies. This is a
    deliberate guard for accounts without an organization and must be included in the authorization review; normal member
    accounts keep their current company-or-creator rule.
    No catch block returns raw database exception text. A runtime failure follows Laravel error handling; no completed
    table is returned for export. Production debug/error handling should follow the existing deployment policy.

    Page 9
    6. Proposed view and export changes
    The proposal keeps browser-side DataTables exports because the current table loads the complete authorized result
    set (serverSide=false). Every format will export all currently filtered rows across all pages, not just the visible page or a
    selected row subset. If server-side paging is introduced later, implement an authorized server export using the same
    query contract; these client options alone cannot export rows that were never loaded.
    The shared business-column list includes one plain Lead Status, Lead Stage Status, giver and receiver company,
    receiver manager, area, ageing, vertical, location, zone, Accepted Date and Remark Histories. It excludes Actions,
    Preview, the editable status cell, and the interactive Remarks icon column. This changes the CSV/XLSX schema
    intentionally; management should approve downstream spreadsheet/import compatibility.
    The action wrapper blocks all formats when input dates differ from applied server dates, when validation fails, or when
    the filtered table has zero rows. Users receive a clear message rather than a misleading stale file or empty download.
    XLSX requires browser JSZip; no PHP Zip/GD installation is required for this browser-based export. CSV remains
    available if only JSZip fails.
    Filename dates come from the applied server range, not editable draft fields. Filenames identify the date range but do
    not encode every dropdown/global search; the exported rows still honor those active client filters. Both formats use a
    common text formatter, remove HTML, and prefix spreadsheet-formula-like text. The older installed Buttons version
    does not support the newer escapeExcelFormula setting, so the formatter implements this explicitly.
    The custom action signature targets the observed Buttons 2.3.2 API. An upgrade to a newer major version must
    re-check its action callback and asynchronous behavior. Existing numeric-looking strings and leading zeros need
    round-trip tests in Excel; a fully typed workbook schema is outside this proposal.

        public function leadbasic()
        {
            $fromdate = config('globalConfig.defalutDateforLeads');
            $request = new \Illuminate\Http\Request([
                'fromdate'   => $fromdate,
                'todate' => date('Y-m-d')
            ]);
            $input['fromdate'] =  $fromdate;
            $input['todate'] =  $request['todate'];
    
            $orgId = Auth()->user()->orgId;
            try {
                if (Auth()->user()->roleId == 1) {
                    $leads = Lead::join('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('requirements_details', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->whereBetween('leads.created_at', [$fromdate . ' 00:00:00', date('Y-m-d') . ' 23:59:59'])
                        ->select('leads.id AS LId', 'leads.accepted_datetime', 'leads.assigned_user_id', 'leads.assigned_date', 'leads.created_at as Cdate', 'leads.leadStatus', 'leads.lead_remarks', 'leads.lead_reject_remarks', 'leads.lead_status', 'leads.assigned_to', 'leads.assigned_orgid', 'client_details.*', 'requirements_details.*', 'financial_details.*')
                        ->orderBy('leads.id', 'desc')
                        ->get();
                } else {
    
                    $leads = Lead::join('client_details', 'client_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('requirements_details', 'requirements_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
                        ->join('financial_details', 'financial_details.lead_id', '=', 'leads.id')
    
                        ->select('leads.id AS LId', 'leads.accepted_datetime', 'leads.assigned_user_id', 'leads.assigned_date', 'leads.created_at as Cdate', 'leads.leadStatus', 'leads.lead_remarks', 'leads.lead_reject_remarks', 'leads.lead_status', 'leads.assigned_to', 'leads.assigned_orgid', 'client_details.*', 'requirements_details.*', 'financial_details.*')
                        ->orderBy('leads.id', 'desc')
                        ->where('leads.assigned_orgid', $orgId)
                        ->orWhere('leads.user_id', Auth()->user()->id)
                        ->whereBetween('leads.created_at', [$fromdate . ' 00:00:00', date('Y-m-d') . ' 23:59:59'])
                        ->get();
                }
    
                $leadStatus = Lead_status_type::all();
                return view('Leads/newdesign/lead', ['leads' => $leads, 'leadStatus' => $leadStatus, 'input' => $input]);
            } catch (\Exception $e) {
                return $e->getMessage();
            }
        }
